messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SmartRouting error-rate > 5% (routing policy mismatch detected). Auto-created incident INC-2460. Immediate on-call: @oncall-sre.

liz: seeing a surge of 500s and function-call failures starting ~2m ago. Traces show repeated falls back to region eu-west then to quantized-variant that doesn't support tool-calls. Impacting a few customers on Dedicated.

amar: confirmed. Routing logs: policy evaluation returned 'variant_swap' then 'fallback_eu -> quant_q4' repeatedly for same request ids. Looks like fallback throttle is too aggressive and we're swapping variants mid-request.

oncall-sre: I'm on it. Can someone paste the exact routing decision trace for a failing req id?

alex: pasting an anonymized trace (snippet):

```
route_decision: preferred=fp16_v2
policy_eval: latency_sla=10ms -> preferred ok
capacity_check: eu-west no_capacity
fallback: region=eu-west->us-east
variant_swap: select_quant_q4 (tool_call_support=false)
runtime_error: tool_call_missing_support -> 500
```

jane: customer visible symptom: function-call API returns 500 with body: {\"error\":\"model variant does not support tool calling\"}.

eric: that lines up — our compatibility matrix shows quant_q4 has tool_call_support=false for sequences > 1k tokens and when kv-cache used. Looks like the routing code didn't check context_length or tool_call flag.

oncall-sre: mitigation idea: temporarily stop variant swapping on fallbacks and force only fp16 variants for routes where request.metadata.tool_call==true. Can we flip a feature flag?

liz: +1. We should also add a short-circuit to avoid region -> variant oscillation (thundering fallback). Set cooldown on fallback attempts for the same request id.

amar: I can push a hotpatch to the routing policy config: add `fallback.variant_preference = [fp16_v2, fp16_v1]` and `fallback.cooldown_seconds = 30` for smart-routing. Will deploy to staging then prod if green.

oncall-sre: do it. Also, reduce fallback throttle so we don't aggressively overflow other regions.

alex: commands I'll run (prod config update):

```
# lockstep deploy to routing-config service
curl -X POST "https://config-api.internal/v1/policies/smartroute" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" -d '{"fallback":{"variant_preference":["fp16_v2","fp16_v1"],"cooldown_seconds":30}}'
```

jane: pinging affected customers (support) now. Small set: CUST-987, CUST-451 (Dedicated EU). I'll add 'temporary degraded' note.

eric: quick risk note: pinning to fp16 increases token cost ~1.8x for those requests and may slightly raise latency. Customers on Reserved capacity might see throttling — include that in notices.

oncall-sre: deployed new fallback config to prod canary (10% traffic) at +2m. Monitoring.

liz: metrics after canary: error-rate for canary dropped from 6.2% -> 0.6%. No tool-call 500s in canary. Good sign.

amar: rolling to 50% now. Will keep fallback cooldown.

alex: rolling to 100% complete. Verified routing decisions now select fp16 variants when tool_call flag true or context_length > 1024.

oncall-sre: alert suppressed. Closing pager for now but keeping incident open for follow-up.

jane: customer update sent: "We applied a routing configuration change to prevent incompatible model variants from being selected during failover. You may see slightly higher token consumption on a subset of requests; there's no data exposure and we will monitor closely."

eric: next steps: 1) Patch smart-routing to consult compatibility matrix for tool_call and context length before variant selection; 2) Add unit tests for fallbacks that simulate region/full capacity + tool calls; 3) Add telemetry that surfaces when a variant with incompatible capabilities is chosen.

liz: adding those to INC-2460 ticket and assigning owners: Alex -> routing unit tests & config validation, Amar -> compatibility-check hook, Eric -> telemetry/alert, Jane -> customer comms.

oncall-sre: also recommend short blameless postmortem, timeline, and a retro for fallback cooldown defaults.

eric: I'll draft postmortem. Include cost impact estimate and list of affected customers.

jane: retention: I saved relevant logs and created a support thread with customers for follow-up.

liz: final note — random thought: we should treat 'tool_call' as a hard capability during policy evaluation (fail closed) rather than a soft preference. If the model doesn't support it, failover shouldn't select it.

amar: agree. I'll make that change in the policy evaluator.

oncall-sre: thanks everyone. Marking incident INC-2460 as 'mitigated' and leaving 'investigating' for the follow-up tasks. Will hand off to next shift. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2460 state changed to MITIGATED by oncall-sre. Handing off to next oncall.

(End of thread)
